To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hot-carrier immunity of 0.7-0.8- micrometers gate length MOSFETs can be greatly improved by reoxidation of the nitrided gate oxide at 900-1100 degrees C for about 30-60 s, and that this is due to a decrease in the interface state density at midgap and the suppression of the interface-state generation rate at the source and drain junctions.
the reoxidation process markedly improves hot-carier immunity in nitrided oxies, but that a new degradation characteristic inherent to nitrided oxied is also observed.

the hot-carrier-induced threshold shift and degradation of the transconductance in submicrometer n-channel MOSFETs can be significantly improved by reoxidation of nitrided oxdes prepared by rapid thermal annealing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new MOSFET process technology using nitrided oxynitride films prepared by rapid reoxidation.
the fabrication of submicrometer MOS devices using nitrided oxynitrides.
the development of a new process for the fabrication of MOSFETs having a thin nitrided oxide with improved hot-carrier immunity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reoxidized-nitrided oxide process is a promising technique to improve the hot-carrier immunity of submicrometer MOS devices.
reoxidized nitrides are superior to thermal oxides in hot-carrier immunity.
the reoxidized nitrides are superior to thermal oxides in hot-carrier reliability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reoxidized nitride-oxide system has a great advantage for submicrometer MOS device fabrication.
the reoxidized nitride-oxide system is a good compromise between the thermal oxide system and nitrided-oxides system, and that it is a promising material for submicrometer MOS devices.
the reoxidation of nitrided oxdes by rapid thermal processing is an effective technique for the improvement of MOSFET hot-carrier immunity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hot-carrier immunity of MOSFETs is improved by reoxidizing the nitrided oxide, which is a promising approach for submicrometer MOS devices.
the reoxidation of a nitrided oxide can be a very powerful technique to improve hot-carrier immunity.
the hot-carrier lifetime of sub-micron MOSFETs is greatly enhanced by rapid thermal oxidation of a nitrided oxide, which is attributed to the formation of a high density of SiO2/Si interfaces.
